why: The content script runs on every page and, because the manifest sets all_frames, in every frame of it. That weight is a cost the product charges a person for visiting anything, and nothing was watching it: a stray import that pulled the UI graph or the storage layer into this bundle would double it silently, and the only way anyone would find out is by profiling a page one day.
rule: A ten-percent band each way. Outside it, in either direction, the build fails and the number here has to move in the same change — up with an argument, down because the saving is real. The band is not about micro-optimisation: what it exists to catch is an accidental graph, and an unintended import of a package is tens of kilobytes, far outside ten percent.
whyBytesMayGateWhereMillisecondsMayNot: This project refuses to gate on wall-clock ceilings (see the m0/m1 spec and the bench decision): a timing ceiling reddens from runner load rather than from code, which teaches people to ignore it. A byte count is deterministic — the same source produces the same bundle on any machine — so it is exactly the kind of ceiling this project can hold somebody to.
